h1: Uncle Loy's Boutique House — Bangkok's highest-rated small guesthouse, a 9-minute walk from Siriraj Hospital
intro: On a quiet lane tucked beside Wang Lang market, Uncle Loy's Boutique House is a lovingly converted 80-year-old family home with just six rooms — spotlessly clean, with comfortable beds, a freshly made breakfast every morning (including the mango sticky rice guests write home about), and owners who treat every guest like a friend coming to stay. It sits roughly 700 metres from Siriraj Hospital — about a 9-minute walk — making it the most warmly received budget-boutique option for anyone with medical business at Siriraj. Wang Lang/Prannok pier is a short walk away for the Chao Phraya express boat, and Wat Arun is two minutes across the water. From approx. THB 1,200/night.

body.html: Uncle Loy's Boutique House sits on Soi Arun-Ammarin 20 in the Wang Lang–Prannok quarter of Bangkok Noi, on the Thonburi bank of the Chao Phraya. The building goes back to 1936 — over 80 years old — but the interior has been carefully updated to keep the character of the old house (timber proportions, the maze of corridors and rooflines that one guest described as having "a very Japanese feeling") while adding private bathrooms, air-conditioning and Wi-Fi. It is run directly by a family: the owners, known to guests as Bep and her son Gus (Pakawat), appear in dozens of reviews as the main reason people give five stars.

The property has just six rooms — Twin Rooms with two single beds, and Twin Rooms with a private balcony. Every room has a private bathroom with walk-in shower, air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, and free Wi-Fi. The small scale means every room is looked after closely; multiple guests describe arriving to find the room so clean it felt "like sleeping at home." Worth knowing before you book: there is no lift, ground-floor rooms can hear early-morning birdsong, and parking in the narrow lane is very limited — this is not a place to drive to.
"Amazing location for all top attractions in Bangkok — the rooms are clean and tidy, with everything you need. And the mango sticky rice at breakfast is the best I've had in Thailand."

Breakfast is the most talked-about feature in the reviews. It's made fresh to order every morning — eggs, fruit, toast, and Thai specialities including the mango sticky rice that guests mention in review after review. The atmosphere at breakfast is genuinely homey, not a hotel buffet, and several guests say it gave them the "authentic Bangkok" experience they were after. There is also an on-site coffee shop and an outdoor seating area where you can sit with a drink between sightseeing trips.

The location has real strengths and one trade-off worth knowing about. On the plus side: the guesthouse is about 700 metres from Siriraj Hospital — roughly a 9-minute walk — making it one of the most accessible options for patients' families or anyone with medical appointments at Siriraj. Wang Lang/Prannok pier is a 5-minute walk away, giving you easy access to the Chao Phraya express boat: cross to Wat Arun in two minutes, or ride the river to Tha Tian (near Wat Pho) or further north. The MRT Blue Line (Siriraj or Itsaraphap stations) is also reachable on foot or by boat. The trade-off: the area is on the Thonburi bank, in a network of small lanes. Taxis coming from the east side of the river are reluctant to make the journey at night, so if you plan on late evenings out, the boat and metro are the sensible way home.

A score of 9.5 from 455 Booking.com reviews, and a 4.8/5 on TripAdvisor (#127 of 1,421 specialty lodging in Bangkok), is exceptional for a six-room guesthouse. Reviews converge on the same points: the warmth of the family owners, the fresh breakfast, and a location that gives easy access to the river temples. The grumbles that appear occasionally are: a cancelled booking without proper communication (one 2024 review), the difficulty of getting a taxi at night, and the very limited parking. None of these are inherent to the guesthouse itself, but they are worth planning around.

Uncle Loy's is best for: families and friends of patients at Siriraj Hospital who want a warm, affordable alternative to an anonymous medical-district hotel; travellers who want to experience Thonburi's old riverside neighbourhood as it really is; and couples or solo travellers who prefer a small, characterful place over a big chain hotel. Less suitable for: anyone who needs to park a car, anyone who needs 24-hour check-in or full hotel-style facilities, and anyone who plans on returning very late every night.

honestSummary: Uncle Loy's Boutique House delivers genuine family warmth, a great location for Siriraj Hospital, and a freshly made breakfast that guests talk about for weeks. It is not a hotel with full facilities — it's a six-room heritage home run by people who care. Accept that getting back late by taxi can be tricky, that there's no pool, and that you must confirm your reservation in advance.

tips.title: Use the river boat — it beats taxis hands-down
tips.body: Wang Lang/Prannok pier is a 5-minute walk. The Chao Phraya express boat gets you to the Grand Palace area, Tha Tian or Saphan Taksin without traffic. Far quicker than a taxi — especially evenings.

tips.title: Always confirm your booking directly
tips.body: With only 6 rooms, a handful of past guests reported booking issues. Send the owners a message or call to reconfirm 1–2 days before you arrive — it takes 2 minutes and avoids any misunderstanding.

tips.title: Arrive before 22:00
tips.body: Uncle Loy's is a family home, not a 24-hour hotel. Let the owners know your arrival time in advance — if your plans change, message them so they can arrange things. Arriving well before 22:00 is strongly recommended.

tips.title: Do not skip breakfast
tips.body: Freshly made to order every morning: eggs, fresh fruit, mango sticky rice. Guests repeatedly say it's the best breakfast they had in Thailand. Set your alarm — it's worth getting up for.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Uncle Loy's Boutique House Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Uncle Loy's Boutique House and how far is it from Siriraj Hospital?
faq.a: The guesthouse is at 91 Soi Arun-Ammarin 20, Siriraj, Bangkok Noi, Bangkok 10700. It is approximately 700 metres from Siriraj Hospital — about a 9-minute walk. Wang Lang/Prannok pier is a 5-minute walk away for the Chao Phraya express boat, and the MRT Blue Line (Siriraj or Itsaraphap stations) is reachable on foot or by boat.

faq.q: How much does Uncle Loy's Boutique House cost and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at approximately THB 1,200/night for a standard Twin Room with two single beds. Twin Rooms with a private balcony start around THB 1,400. Prices vary by date and package — always compare across platforms before booking. There are only 6 rooms, so book ahead, especially on Thai public holidays.

faq.q: Is Uncle Loy's Boutique House a good option for families visiting a patient at Siriraj?
faq.a: It's one of the best. About a 9-minute walk (~700 m) to Siriraj Hospital, affordable, the owners are warm and genuinely helpful, and breakfast is freshly made every morning. The only caveats are that there's no lift, check-in closes by around 22:00, and you need to confirm your booking in advance.

faq.q: How do you get to Uncle Loy's Boutique House — is the MRT or river boat better?
faq.a: The easiest route is the Chao Phraya express boat to Wang Lang/Prannok pier, then a 5-minute walk. The pier has boats heading upriver (Grand Palace, Tha Tian, Phra Arthit) and downriver (Sathorn/BTS Saphan Taksin). For the MRT Blue Line, the nearest stations are Siriraj and Itsaraphap. Taxis work but can be hard to find in this area late at night — the boat is far more reliable.

faq.q: Does Uncle Loy's Boutique House have a swimming pool or gym?
faq.a: No swimming pool and no gym. This is a six-room boutique guesthouse in a heritage home — it's about personal hospitality, a great location and wonderful breakfast, not resort facilities. If a pool is a must, you'll need a larger hotel on the Sukhumvit or riverside hotel strip instead.

faq.q: Is the breakfast at Uncle Loy's really as good as the reviews say?
faq.a: The short answer: yes. Breakfast is made fresh to order every morning — eggs, fresh fruit, and Thai dishes including mango sticky rice. Multiple guests say it was the best breakfast they had anywhere in Thailand. It may be included in some packages or charged separately — ask when booking. Either way, don't skip it.
